questions.q: Why is CSDM adoption normally phased rather than attempted all at once?
options: A big-bang, all-at-once cutover is always faster and simpler
Real organizations already have thousands of CIs and services with no formal record, so phasing delivers usable value in stages instead
ServiceNow technically prevents applying CSDM to more than one service at a time
Phasing is only a formality with no real practical benefit
questions.explain: Trying to map an entire existing estate into CSDM in one pass is rarely how real implementations succeed.

questions.q: What should a sensible phase one of a CSDM rollout start with?
options: Documenting every network device in the data center
Identifying and documenting the organization's most critical Business Services first
Deleting CIs that don't yet have a Technical Service assigned
Writing custom integrations for every ServiceNow module
questions.explain: Phase one works top-down, starting with the handful of Business Services where an outage is expensive or highly visible.

questions.q: How is "most critical" typically judged when choosing which Business Services to model first?
options: By a mix of revenue impact, customer visibility, and regulatory exposure — not by which service is easiest to model
By which service has the fewest underlying CIs
By alphabetical order of service name
By which service's Technical Service happens to already exist
questions.explain: Criticality is judged by real business impact, not by convenience or ease of modeling.

questions.q: After naming the priority Business Services, what does the next phase do?
options: Immediately deploys new infrastructure for each service
Identifies the Technical Services that actually deliver each priority Business Service
Skips straight to documenting every CI in the environment
Removes the Business Service layer entirely since it's no longer needed
questions.explain: This is the step where IT and the business connect: naming the technical capability, like an application stack, that delivers each named Business Service.

questions.q: Why does this lesson argue that a bottom-up approach — cataloging every CI first — is a costly mistake?
options: Because CIs cannot be created before a Business Service exists
Because it is technically impossible in ServiceNow
Because months of inventory work can end up reorganized or discarded once service priorities are finally set, and the payoff is delayed
Because bottom-up inventories are always less accurate than top-down ones
questions.explain: Going top-down ties CMDB work to business value from day one; bottom-up risks a lot of rework once real priorities emerge.
